2016 League of Legends World Championship :: Background :: chunk_0001
After the [2015 *League of Legends* World Championship](/wiki/2015_League_of_Legends_World_Championship "2015 League of Legends World Championship") was held across Europe, the 2016 edition was held in North America.[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3)

The original prize pool was $2.13 million contributed by [Riot Games](/wiki/Riot_Games "Riot Games"), with the final amount being calculated after fan contributions stopped on November 6.[[4]](#cite_note-espn2016-4) Riot pledged to add 25% of all revenue generated from [selling](/wiki/Microtransaction "Microtransaction") Championship wards and skins – customizations for the player controlled hero character – to the prize pool.[[5]](#cite_note-:0-5) On October 28, the sale of these unique Championship skins had grown the prize pool to $5.07 million, making it the largest single prize pool in *League of Legends* history.[[6]](#cite_note-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7) The final prize pool reached $6.7 million.[[8]](#cite_note-concurrent-8) Riot announced that 40% of the prize pool will be awarded to the winning team and 15% to the runner up.[[4]](#cite_note-espn2016-4) The winning team would also receive 25% of revenue from skins created to commemorate the championship victory.[[5]](#cite_note-:0-5)

To encourage new viewers to watch, Riot Games set up a second stream specifically for new viewers, which would help explain basic game concepts that more experienced viewers on the regular stream would be familiar with.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

Riot Games collaborated with [Zedd](/wiki/Zedd "Zedd"), an [electronic dance music](/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music") [disc jockey](/wiki/Disc_jockey "Disc jockey") to create "Ignite", a dance music anthem for the tournament. The video referenced multiple highlights from previous *League of Legends* world championships.[[10]](#cite_note-10) As of July 2022, it has almost 90 million views on [YouTube](/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[[11]](#cite_note-11)

Lithium reacts with water easily, but with noticeably less vigor than other alkali metals. The reaction forms [hydrogen](/wiki/Hydrogen "Hydrogen") gas and [lithium hydroxide](/wiki/Lithium_hydroxide "Lithium hydroxide").[[11]](#cite_note-krebs-11) When placed over a flame, lithium compounds give off a striking crimson color, but when the metal burns strongly, the flame becomes a brilliant silver. Lithium will ignite and burn in oxygen when exposed to water or water vapor. In moist air, lithium rapidly tarnishes to form a black coating of [lithium hydroxide](/wiki/Lithium_hydroxide "Lithium hydroxide") (LiOH and LiOH·H2O), [lithium nitride](/wiki/Lithium_nitride "Lithium nitride") (Li3N) and [lithium carbonate](/wiki/Lithium_carbonate "Lithium carbonate") (Li2CO3, the result of a secondary reaction between LiOH and [CO2](/wiki/Carbon_dioxide "Carbon dioxide")).[[40]](#cite_note-kamienski-40) Lithium is one of the few metals that react with [nitrogen](/wiki/Nitrogen "Nitrogen") gas.[[91]](#cite_note-92)[[92]](#cite_note-93)

Because of its reactivity with water, and especially nitrogen, lithium metal is usually stored in a hydrocarbon sealant, often [petroleum jelly](/wiki/Petroleum_jelly "Petroleum jelly"). Although the heavier alkali metals can be stored under [mineral oil](/wiki/Mineral_oil "Mineral oil"), lithium is not dense enough to fully submerge itself in these liquids.[[35]](#cite_note-emsley-35)

[Arctic vegetation](/wiki/Arctic_vegetation "Arctic vegetation") is composed of plants such as [dwarf shrubs](/wiki/Subshrub "Subshrub"), [graminoids](/wiki/Graminoid "Graminoid"), [herbs](/wiki/Herb "Herb"), [lichens](/wiki/Lichen "Lichen"), and [mosses](/wiki/Moss "Moss"), which all grow relatively close to the ground, forming [tundra](/wiki/Tundra "Tundra"). An example of a dwarf shrub is the [bearberry](/wiki/Bearberry "Bearberry"). As one moves northward, the amount of warmth available for plant growth decreases considerably. In the northernmost areas, plants are at their metabolic limits, and small differences in the total amount of summer warmth make large differences in the amount of energy available for maintenance, growth, and reproduction. Colder summer temperatures cause the size, abundance, productivity, and variety of plants to decrease. Trees cannot grow in the Arctic, but in its warmest parts, shrubs are common and can reach 2 m (6 ft 7 in) in height; [sedges](/wiki/Cyperaceae "Cyperaceae"), mosses and lichens can form thick layers. In the coldest parts of the Arctic, much of the ground is bare; [non-vascular plants](/wiki/Non-vascular_plant "Non-vascular plant") such as lichens and mosses predominate, along with a few scattered grasses and [forbs](/wiki/Forb "Forb") (like the [Arctic poppy](/wiki/Papaver_radicatum "Papaver radicatum")).

At that point, it had the biggest pre-opening of any film, breaking the six-year record held by *[Die Hard 2](/wiki/Die_Hard_2 "Die Hard 2")*. The next day on July 3, the film officially opened to the public with $17.4 million.[[69]](#cite_note-69) During its second day of release, it earned $17.3 million, which made it the highest Thursday gross, holding this record for six years until it was taken by *[Star Wars: Episode II – Attack of the Clones](/wiki/Star_Wars:_Episode_II_%E2%80%93_Attack_of_the_Clones "Star Wars: Episode II – Attack of the Clones")* in 2002.[[70]](#cite_note-70) This was also the highest non-sequel Thursday gross, which would last until the opening of *[Transformers](/wiki/Transformers_(film) "Transformers (film)")* in 2007.[[71]](#cite_note-71) *Independence Day* earned $104.3 million in its opening week,[[72]](#cite_note-EW4-72) including $96.1 million during its five-day holiday opening, and $50.2 million during its opening weekend.[[73]](#cite_note-numbers-73) The film stayed in the number-one spot for three consecutive weeks before being displaced by *[A Time to Kill](/wiki/A_Time_to_Kill_(1996_film) "A Time to Kill (1996 film)")*.[[74]](#cite_note-74)[[2]](#cite_note-BOM-2) Moreover, it beat *[Terminator 2: Judgment Day](/wiki/Terminator_2:_Judgment_Day "Terminator 2: Judgment Day")*'s record for largest five-day Wednesday gross of any film, as well as the biggest July opening weekend.[[75]](#cite_note-75) The combined total for the five-day Wednesday opening with ticket sales increased
